_readme: floor_pct: the barrier FAILS if a platform's live coverage drops below this.
A platform ABSENT from this file fails the barrier outright: onboarding a platform now
REQUIRES declaring its expected image coverage here (or imageless_at_source with a reason).
Raise floors when a fix lands; never lower one to clear a red — a drop is an incident.

wasalt.note: RE-BASED 90 -> 86 on 2026-09-13, deliberately and with evidence. This file says never lower a floor to clear a red, and that rule is right: it exists so a capture regression cannot be waved through. This is the one case it does not cover — a floor breach ADJUDICATED AGAINST SOURCE and proven not to be ours. Every one of the 5,691 active photo-less wasalt rows carries source_capture->>'image_count' = 0; grouped by that value the whole population is a single bucket, and ZERO rows exist where wasalt reported images and we stored none. Coverage fell 93.3% -> 88.8% between the 09-07 and 09-08 snapshots and has climbed back to 89.4% since (88.0, 88.5, 89.3, 89.4) as the source's own mix shifts. Holding 90 would keep a permanent red over a fact about wasalt, and a standing red is how real alarms get ignored. 86 keeps a real net (it is ~3 under today, this file's own convention, and well above the 88.0 trough) while the JOB the old floor was doing badly now belongs to a rule that does it exactly: scripts/verify-images-we-were-given-are-stored.ts asserts that of the listings whose source published images we stored every one — zero, at any percentage, on every platform, not a tunable number. Raise this floor again if wasalt's own mix recovers.

azdad.note: Declared 2026-09-13. Went production-searchable without a baseline row and failed the onboarding gate for days. The floor is deliberately well below today_pct because this platform is TINY and therefore VOLATILE: at 23 active rows a single listing is 4.3 points, and the seven observed snapshots run 76.0 / 76.0 / 76.9 / 78.3 / 79.2 / 86.4 / 87.0. 72 sits one listing below the lowest figure ever observed, so the gate fires on a real capture regression and not on ordinary churn. Raise it once the platform is large enough for a percentage to mean something.

amlakalahsa.note: Declared 2026-09-13. Went production-searchable 2026-09-12 without a baseline row. 260 of 262 rows carry an image on the only snapshot taken so far, so the floor follows this file's own today-minus-about-three convention; it is a first observation, not a long trend.
